findings.conclusion: unlink_if_present returns true only after remove_file succeeds, false only for NotFound, and propagates every other IO error as CcError::Io. Object, half and temp deletion branches use this result.

Both unlink attempts must complete successfully before object counters can be returned; at least one actual unlink is required to increment. First-half failure stops before its counterpart; second-half failure can leave first half removed. Err returns no counters, without claiming rollback or zero work.

run_gc_pass uses ? on sweep before constructing the next cursor, so an error cannot return an advanced cursor. Recovery fixtures restore the failing path and call fresh collect/run_gc_pass; a surviving second half is reclassified and counted as a half. This cursor error contract is a code-path review, not an injected failure inside run_gc_pass.
The change does not mutate DB or generation, and leaves mark/freshness/pair protection and bounded collection logic unchanged. The original semantic_gc test file is byte-identical to base.

Read all five fixed test functions: four real directory-at-file unlink failures plus a four-seed absent-half/idempotence control. Fixtures use owned temporary files and the public collect/sweep boundary; no permissions, provider, process kill or hidden production hook. Module/test/checkpoint docs explicitly retain the collection/mark/unlink race limitation.
